All of this is in `src/tessel/views.py`:

1. **`VerbView.__init_subclass__`** (line 165) runs when you define a subclass such as `CounterAPI`. It scans `http_method_funcs` for names the class defines (`get`, `post`, …) and sets `cls.methods = {"GET", "POST"}`. It also merges in `methods` from base classes.

2. **`View.to_view_func(name, ...)`** (line 86, classmethod) builds the plain view function `view(**kwargs)`:
   - If `init_every_request` is true, it creates a new `view_class(...)` instance per request. Otherwise it reuses one shared instance.
   - Either way it calls `active_app.ensure_sync(self.run_view)(**kwargs)`.
   - It applies `cls.decorators` and attaches `view_class`, `methods` and `provide_automatic_options` to the function. The route registration reads these attributes, so the rule only accepts the allowed methods.

3. **`VerbView.run_view`** (line 182) does the per-method routing:
   - It looks up `getattr(self, request.method.lower())`, so a GET request goes to `get()` and a POST request to `post()`.
   - A `HEAD` request falls back to `get()` if there is no `head()`.
   - It asserts if there is no handler, and calls the handler through `ensure_sync` with the URL kwargs.

`View.run_view` (line 78) is the abstract hook, and `VerbView` overrides it. You register the result with `app.attach_route_rule("/counter", view_func=CounterAPI.to_view_func("counter"))`.
